disposition_reason: Total filtered iron in 85 tubewell drinking-water samples: range, median, IQR, mean and concentration-class summaries.

study.design: cross-sectional drinking-water survey with hazard-quotient screening
study.method: HACH FerroVer method 8008 on DR/3900 spectrophotometer after 1.0 um glass microfiber filtration; acidified samples
lod: Method range 0.02 to 3.0 mg/L for iron (Methods p. 2)
study.qa: Reagent blanks and replicate samples; no reference material reported

findings.group: 85 arsenic-safe public tubewells, one per union, Jashore district, Bangladesh, Jan to Mar 2017
findings.notes: Median of filtered total iron; IQR 0.27 to 2.47 mg/L; range 0.02 to 6.2 mg/L.

findings.group: 85 arsenic-safe public tubewells, one per union, Jashore district, Bangladesh, Jan to Mar 2017

findings.notes: Maximum; exceeds the stated upper method range of 3.0 mg/L, dilution not described.

unresolved: Manganese results not recorded as findings (outside this element).
regulatory_or_exposure: WHO aesthetic value for iron in drinking water 0.3 mg/L, as cited by the paper (p. 1 to 2)
Bangladesh drinking-water standard for iron 0.3 to 1.0 mg/L, as cited (p. 2)
2.0 mg/L iron cut-off described as 10% of a JECFA provisional maximum tolerable daily intake of 0.8 mg/kg bw (60 kg, 2 L/day), as cited (p. 3)
Oral reference dose 0.7 mg/kg/day attributed to US EPA 2006 provisional value, used for HQ (p. 3)
Adult iron HQ 0.004 to 1.446 (median 0.161), above 1 at 7 wells; child HQ 0.002 to 0.590 (median 0.066) (p. 6; Fig. 6)
Iron plus manganese HI above 1 at 33 wells for adults and 3 wells for children (p. 7; Fig. 7)
non_numeric_findings: About 73% of wells exceeded the Bangladesh iron limit.
Only about 5% of the groundwater surface area was in the minimal class for both iron and manganese.
Arsenic was not re-measured; the 'safe' cut-off is printed as 0.05 mg/L in Methods and 0.005 mg/L in Limitations.
No correlation between iron and manganese across wells.
